test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 8 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 9(1/3)​ hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for pump (A) = 8 hr

Time for pump + leak (A − B) = 28/3 hr

Total Capacity (LCM of 8, 28) = 56 units

Efficiency of Leak (B) = (56 ÷ 8) − (56 ÷ (28/3)) = 7 − 6 = 1 unit/hr

Time for Leak to empty = 56 ÷ 1 = 56 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 56 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling time of **Electric Pump** (P) = 8 hours

Filling time with **Leakage** (P + L) = 9(1/3) hours = 28/3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

 **Component**
 **Time (hr)**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**

 Pump (P)
 8
 56 units
 7

 Pump + Leak (P + L)
 28/3
 6

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Pump (P) = 56 ÷ 8 = 7 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of (Pump + Leak) = 56 ÷ (28/3) = (56 × 3) ÷ 28 = 2 × 3 = 6 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of Leak (L) = Efficiency of (P + L) − Efficiency of P

⇒ Efficiency of Leak (L) = 6 − 7 = −1 unit/hr (Negative sign denotes emptying)

⇒ Time taken by Leak to empty the tank = Total Capacity ÷ |Efficiency of Leak|

⇒ Time = 56 ÷ 1 = 56 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 56 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

Filling pipes have positive efficiency, while leakage or outlet pipes have negative efficiency.

Leakage Formula

If a pipe fills a tank in 'x' hours and with a leak it takes 'y' hours, the leak empties it in (xy) ÷ (y − x) hours.

Total Work (Capacity)

LCM of individual time durations is the most efficient way to assume the total capacity of the tank.</p
